summary.oneLiner: An independent power producer running hydro and supercritical thermal plants in Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh, backed by a captive coal mine and long-term PPAs, while exiting non-core coal-mining and cement-grinding activities.
summary.business: Jaiprakash Power Ventures is engaged in thermal and hydro power generation supported by coal mining and cement grinding. It owns and operates three power plants aggregating 2,220 MW, selling power to state distribution companies under long-term PPAs and the balance as merchant power on exchanges and bilateral basis. Its captive coal mine feeds the Nigrie thermal plant, while its cement-grinding unit remained idle and is being positioned for exit.

currentContext.strengths: Long-term power purchase agreements with state discoms (UPPCL, MPPMCL) provide assured baseload offtake for the hydro and thermal fleet|Captive Amelia (North) coal mine supplies fuel to the Nigrie supercritical plant, reducing fuel-sourcing risk|High plant availability and improving plant load factors across the thermal fleet (Nigrie PLF 88.79%, Bina PLF 75.21% in FY25-26)|Both Bina and Nigrie thermal plants fall under Category-C and are compliant with SO2 emission norms without requiring FGD installation, avoiding related capex
currentContext.strategies: No dividend recommended by the Board for FY2025-26. The Company (within the top 500 listed entities by market capitalisation as on 31.03.2026) maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy hosted on its website. No amounts were pending for transfer to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF), and no shares were required to be transferred to IEPF during the year.|Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD): minimizing wastewater discharge and maximizing recycling treated as a key environmental priority for the water-intensive thermal power operations.|Early Warning System (EWS) and Automatic Weather Station (AWS) developed jointly with Jaypee University (research by JUET Guna) to give advance information of river flooding and align with Dam Safety Act 2021 requirements.|All sites are ISO 45001 certified for occupational health and safety, with focus on workforce training to avoid accidents and human losses.|Waste management strategy to reduce, reuse and recycle ash and other wastes generated from thermal power plants.|Hazardous waste from all JPVL sites disposed in accordance with regulatory requirements.|Reasonable assurance of the BRSR Core obtained (assurance provider: KSV AMRIT Social Asia), with disclosures on a consolidated basis covering plants, offices and subsidiary companies.
currentContext.expansion: Jaiprakash Power Ventures owns and operates three power plants with an aggregate capacity of 2220 MW, a 2 MTPA Cement Grinding Unit and a 3.92 MTPA coal mine. The generating assets are the 400 MW Vishnuprayag Hydro-Electric Plant in Uttarakhand (in operation since October 2006, 88% supplied to UPPCL under PPA and 12% free to the Government of Uttarakhand), the 500 MW (2x250 MW) Jaypee Bina Thermal Power Plant at Sirchopi, District Sagar, Madhya Pradesh (units commissioned August 2012 and April 2013, 70% of installed capacity tied to MPPMCL long-term with the balance sold as merchant power), and the 1320 MW (2x660 MW) Jaypee Nigrie Supercritical Thermal Power Plant at Nigrie, Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh (units commissioned September 2014 and February 2015, part-merchant via IEX, HPX and PXIL). Coal for Nigrie comes from the captive Amelia (North) Coal Mine (operating at its peak rated capacity of 2.8 MTPA since 2015), and the adjacent partially-explored Bandha North Coal Block was allocated to the Company under commercial-mining revenue-sharing. The report describes contraction rather than expansion: after the financial-year close the Board decided to surrender both the Amelia (North) and Bandha North coal mines, citing recent changes in Government coal policies, economic viability and sociological aspects, with the surrender process under progress subject to requisite approvals. The 2 MTPA Jaypee Nigrie Cement Grinding Unit (commercial operations since 3rd June 2015) produced no cement in FY2025-26 owing to clinker supply constraints, and the Company continues to explore ways to exit this non-core cement-grinding activity. Following an MoEF&CC notification dated July 11, 2025 exempting Category-C plants from sulphur-dioxide emission standards, both Bina and Nigrie TPPs were held to require no FGD installation, and a Settlement Agreement was executed with GEPIL in October 2025 to foreclose the FGD contract.

risks.risk: Erratic offtake / restricted dispatch by MPPMCL at Bina TPP
risks.note: MPPMCL gives restricted, erratic and fluctuating dispatch schedules to Bina TPP, sometimes scheduling very low offtake, which renders it technically unfeasible to run the plant optimally and forces the Company to sell balance power on exchanges at un-remunerative tariffs.

A large share of Nigrie and Bina generation is sold as merchant power on energy exchanges and bilateral arrangements (e.g. 5,799.24 MUs merchant sales at Nigrie), leaving realizations exposed to volatile short-term power market prices rather than long-term PPA tariffs.

risks.risk: Hydrology dependence at Vishnuprayag hydro plant
risks.note: Vishnuprayag Hydro Electric Power Plant generation is dependent on river flows; FY26 generation was lower than the prior year due to hydrology, making this run-of-river asset's output structurally weather/monsoon dependent.

risks.risk: Surrender of captive coal mines / coal supply security
risks.note: Post year-end the Board decided to surrender the Amelia (North) and Bandha North coal mines citing recent changes in Government coal policies, economic viability and sociological aspects; the surrender is subject to requisite approvals and affects the captive coal linkage that fed Nigrie plant.

risks.risk: Flexible operation stress from rising renewables
risks.note: Increasing renewable generation reduces daytime power demand from thermal plants, forcing thermal machines to operate at lower generation to meet SLDC/WRLDC schedules, which creates stresses in the boiler-turbine-generator (BTG) systems.

risks.risk: Environmental and water compliance (ZLD, hazardous waste, emissions)
risks.note: Thermal operations require significant water and generate effluent, ash and hazardous waste; non-compliance with water discharge, Zero Liquid Discharge and waste standards carries regulatory penalties, environmental liabilities and reputational risk.

Difficulty obtaining spares or support for equipment and systems installed at the time of plant commissioning is flagged as a risk, mitigated by maintaining sufficient spares, in-house repair strength and technology upgrades.

Cyberattack is flagged as a global threat to major industrial organizations including generating plants; the Company relies on GoI requirements and a Group CISO monitoring internal and external factors.
